pencereler.0-5: A small military reactor in Idaho exploded during maintenance. In an instant, all three
pencereler.5-12: men working on it were killed. They were reconnecting its central control rod. That rod had to be lifted
pencereler.12-20: by hand. It was pulled far too high. The reactor went critical and flashed water to steam. The blast lifted the reactor
pencereler.20-30: vessel off its mounts. Reactors were then designed so no single rod can do this.

bulgular: 12-20s: no central mystery or problem is posed

segmentler.metin: The SL-1 reactor exploded during maintenance.
It took only a single control rod pulled out too far by hand.
So how could a single control rod pulled out too far by hand do this?
The answer is prompt criticality from manual withdrawal of the central control rod, causing a steam explosion — and it is why reactors were designed so no single rod can make them critical.
